assertion.objects: The actual T=T2(E) of the fixed characteristic-zero elliptic curve, its finite reductions, and extension to the actual coefficient ring Ri.
assertion.hypotheses: E is the fixed elliptic curve overQ; use its genuine Tate lattice, compatible finite reductions and cyclotomic pairing. Conjugation and the scalar-character cancellation are separate existing consumer data.
assertion.quantifiers: Every finite coefficient stage i and all vectors in the stated modules.
assertion.uniformity: Compatible with the multiplication maps defining the Tate inverse limit.
assertion.normalizations: The source pairing remains cyclotomic. The consumer composes the second factor with rho_T(tau); no ordinary self-duality of a nonquadratic scalar twist is asserted.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No assertion for torsion order divisible by positive characteristic; no generic-isogeny pairing remark is used.
assertion.limit_order: Use the compatible finite perfect pairing, pass to T2, then extend scalars and apply the actual conjugation operator.
assertion.statement: The actual Tate lattice has an integral perfect cyclotomic Weil pairing, whose scalar extension supplies the pairing input used in the conjugate coefficient construction at3682–3692.

use.reason: Supplies the original elliptic pairing before the existing local conjugate-module construction.

supplier.statement: Finite Weil pairings are bilinear, alternating, nondegenerate and Galois equivariant; their compatible inverse limit gives the corresponding Tate-module pairing.

available_assertion.limit_order: Form compatible finite torsion pairings before passing to the Tate module.
